t: No part of the funds appropriated in this Act for construction of space transportation system facilities at Vandenberg Air Force Base, California, may be obligated until the first rollout of the Space Shuttle has been accomplished.

fable.w: This is a funding limitation that conditions the obligation of construction funds on a programmatic milestone, the first Space Shuttle rollout. The only tempting reading is that the condition works like a pre-decision procedural step, but it involves no consultation, hearing, comment, advisory body, or right to sue for any party outside the federal government. No outside actor takes part in any federal decision here.
fable.s: may be obligated until the first rollout of the Space Shuttle has been accomplished

qwen_block.w: This section imposes a condition on the obligation of federal funds based on a specific operational milestone (the rollout of the Space Shuttle). It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making input from parties outside the federal government. The actors involved are the federal government (appropriating funds) and the federal agency managing the Space Shuttle program. There is no public comment period, advisory board with outside members, or consultation with states or tribes.
qwen_block.s: No part of the funds appropriated in this Act for construction of space transportation system facilities at Vandenberg Air Force Base, California, may be obligated until the first rollout of the Space Shuttle has been accomplished.

opus.w: This provision only says when appropriated funds may be committed: not until the first Space Shuttle rollout. One could read any condition on a federal decision as participation. But this condition is a physical milestone, not consultation with, input from, or a challenge by anyone outside the federal government. Nothing in the section involves participation.
